messages:
maya: heads up — saw a weird provisioning gap after last night's KMS key rotation. some users got created but roles are missing, looks like SCIM retries happened during idp heartbeat window.
paul: ugh. any obvious errors in the scim-provisioner logs?
maya: here's the snippet i grabbed from the repro cluster:
```
2026-03-19T22:04:12Z scim-provisioner INFO start sync for org 123
2026-03-19T22:04:13Z scim-provisioner WARN KMS decrypt failed: decryption error, retrying
2026-03-19T22:04:15Z scim-provisioner INFO created user u-789
2026-03-19T22:04:15Z scim-provisioner ERROR attach-role failed: idp-heartbeat-mismatch
2026-03-19T22:04:16Z scim-provisioner INFO retrying attach-role
```
maya: attach-role kept failing for ~30s then succeeded on retry but some downstream webhooks never fired, so RBAC entries were inconsistent.
trevor: is the idp-heartbeat-mismatch from the idp side or our shim? looks like our agent refuses role attach if heartbeat stale.
idp-bot: observed IdP heartbeat jitter across a few regions during KMS rotation window. latency spike ~45s between metadata fetches.
sec-eng: KMS rotation should be transparent — but if the client can't decrypt cached signing certs, the SP verification can fail. did the rotation change key aliases or ciphertext format?
jessica: rotation was staged with alias swap at 22:03UTC, zero-downtime intended. looks like some nodes still had old ciphertext in memory.
infra-bot: we rolled the keystore on the private plane in two waves (az1 then az2). az2 nodes saw a delay in updating the secret, ~35s.
paul: ok hypothesis: some provisioner instances attempted operations while their local KMS cache couldn't decrypt the IdP metadata/signing key, causing verification to fail -> idp-heartbeat-mismatch -> attach-role aborted but user creation succeeded. that leaves a partial-provision state.
maya: yep that matches what we saw. question: how to make this safer short-term? can we gate role attachment behind a reconciliation loop instead of a strict single-run attach?
trevor: put role attach into the eventual-reconcile queue and mark user as 'provisioned-pending-roles'. then reconcile runs until success. also add backoff and alert when a bunch of users stuck >5m.
sec-eng: add audit-marker logs for partial-provision events and include KMS-key-version and idp-heartbeat-timestamp in the audit entry.
jessica: i'll open a PR to add the reconcile flag + audit fields. also we should change the KMS rotation runbook: swap aliases across all planes, then trigger a smooth rolling restart of provisioners after confirming secret refresh.
infra-bot: recommended runbook patch: pause provisioners, rotate alias, resume with health-check waits. will draft in runbooks repo.
paul: temporary mitigation: run a backfill job to scan for users created in the window 22:03-22:06 and force re-attach roles. i can run this now if ops approves.
maya: please do. i'll capture the user list and give to you. also filing an incident note with timeline and corrective actions.
sec-eng: add an alert for KMS-decrypt-errors >5/min across provisioners (sev2). we want an early signal before RBAC inconsistencies.
jessica: FYI i'll include a KMS key-version header in provisioning events so we can trace which key was active when creation happened.
paul: running backfill now, will post results when done.
infra-bot: backfill job enqueued by ops@pager at 22:30 UTC
paul: backfill finished — fixed 42 users, flagged 3 accounts for manual review (external group mappings). all good for now.
maya: thanks everyone. next steps: PR for reconcile + audit, runbook update, add decrypt-error alert, and postmortem draft in #postmortems.
sec-eng: assigning owners: jessica -> provisioner PR, infra -> runbook, paul -> backfill and alert rule, maya -> postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:
trevor: also recommend a small change to client: treat idp-heartbeat-mismatch as transient and don't abort the whole transaction; prefer eventual consistent state.
maya: agreed. i'll note that in the PR description.
